text: [3:284] “Administration”: “Administration” means: — providing information to employees and beneficiaries with respect to program eligibility and scope; — handling records in connection with the employee benefit program (but not handling payroll deductions); and — effecting, continuing or terminating an employee's participation in any benefit included in the program. [CG 04 35 02 02, ¶ H.1.] (1) [3:284.1] Not discretionary decisions: The purpose of EBL coverage is to protect against ministerial mistakes in administering the plan. “Administration” does not cover liability incurred in discretionary, decision-making activities, such as managing a pension plan's investments. [Maryland Cas. Co. v. Economy Bookbinding Corp. Pension Plan & Trust (D NJ 1985) 621 F.Supp. 410, 413] d. [3:285] Compare—matters excluded: The limited nature of EBL coverage is demonstrated by the following: (1) [3:285.1] No coverage for breach of fiduciary duty: The policy specifically excludes liability for breach of fiduciary duty under ERISA or similar state laws. [CG 04 35 03 05, ¶ A.2.g.] Coverage under other insurance forms: Other insurance forms may cover breach of fiduciary duty.
